topic: motorola edge 70 fusion battery life review
headline_marked: Motorola Edge 70 Fusion: [[A Battery Life Superstar]] With a Massive 7,000mAh Cell
headline: Motorola Edge 70 Fusion: A Battery Life Superstar With a Massive 7,000mAh Cell
summary: This £380/$500 smartphone boasts an incredible 7,000mAh battery, promising up to three days of use on a single charge. It also features a 50MP main camera and IP68 water resistance.
details: The Motorola Edge 70 Fusion is a standout device for those plagued by battery anxiety. It packs a massive 7,000mAh battery, offering exceptional longevity that can easily last two to three days of moderate to heavy use, including gaming and benchmarking.

Priced at £380 (around $500) for the 8GB/256GB model, the Edge 70 Fusion offers a compelling package for its cost. It features a 50-megapixel main camera and a 13MP wide-angle lens, along with an IP68 and IP69 dust and water resistance rating and MIL-STD-810H toughness certification.

While the phone excels in battery life, it's not without its quirks. The design features curved edges that some may find uncomfortable, and charging speeds can be inconsistent. The device only reaches about 25W, significantly lower than the advertised 68W, and a dedicated Motorola charger is recommended for optimal performance.

The Motorola Edge 70 Fusion is not officially available in the US, but can be found in the UK and other global markets, potentially under a different name. Motorola also frequently offers discounts, so keep an eye out for deals before purchasing.

topic: ubisoft co-founder claude guillemot dies in plane crash
headline_marked: Ubisoft co-founder Claude Guillemot [[dies in plane crash]] in France
headline: Ubisoft co-founder Claude Guillemot dies in plane crash in France
summary: Claude Guillemot, 69, was one of two victims in a Cessna 421 crash near La Baule airport on June 19.
details: Ubisoft has confirmed the death of Claude Guillemot, one of the five brothers who co-founded the video game giant in 1986. He was 69 years old.

The accident occurred on June 19 in a field near La Baule airport on France's western coast. The Cessna 421 aircraft was reportedly on fire upon arrival of emergency responders, with the flames spreading to the surrounding environment.

Claude Guillemot was also the chairman and CEO of Guillemot Corp., which owns notable brands like Hercules and Thrustmaster. He served on Ubisoft's board of directors, while his brother Yves remains the company's director, chairman, and CEO.
Under the Guillemot brothers' leadership, Ubisoft grew into a major global publisher, known for popular franchises such as Assassin's Creed and Far Cry.
